Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate you walking through the onboarding timeline. A quick follow-up from our side: we need to split Milestone 2 (Integration & Validation) into two deliverables — 2a (Integration) and 2b (Live Validation window) — because our compliance team requires a staged validation gate.

- Can Redwood provide a change order that captures the split and the adjusted acceptance criteria (we'll need the acceptance window clarified for the Validation phase)?
- Please surface the pricing impact (if any) and any dependency that would push the go-live date. We've attached the current SOW with inline comments.

We'd like to keep the same overall spend band but are open to fee reallocation across milestones rather than an overall increase. If there are SLA implications (especially around acceptance triggers), highlight those — our legal will want any MSA footnote called out explicitly.

Maya / Vivek — looping in legal/contracting perspective here. High-level notes from legal:

- If Milestone 2b changes the effective acceptance criteria, we prefer not to bake that into an ancillary email. Best practice is either: (A) an explicit short footnote to the MSA referencing the Order Form amendment, or (B) an Exhibit on the Order Form that enumerates the new acceptance tests and the Validation window.
- For compliance-driven staged validation, we need to preserve the original SLA remedies unless the parties explicitly reallocate acceptance risks (i.e., if you want the Validation window to reduce Redwood's uptime obligations during validation, that must be spelled out).

Proposed MSA footnote (draft to consider):
"For the purposes of Order Form GW-2026-0953, Milestone 2 shall be bifurcated into 2a and 2b. Validation activities performed under 2b shall not be deemed Customer acceptance for SLA breach purposes unless acceptance criteria in Exhibit X are satisfied. Any changes to SLA remedies remain subject to mutual written agreement."

I'll attach a redline skeleton for the Order Form that places the acceptance language in an Exhibit and adds a cross-reference footnote into the MSA. Vivek / Laura — please flag if this approach hits commercial constraints.

Attachments: Redline_OrderForm_DRAFT.docx (docx)

—Jordan
Director, Contracts & Sales Operations
